\section{A one-condition exponential rejection obstruction outside rank one}

Let $X$ be $p$-by-$2$ and $Y$ be $2$-by-$2$ over $\F_2$, with target zero.
Of the sixteen $Y$, one has rank zero, nine rank one, and six rank two.
The full zero-product fiber has size
\[
 2^{2p}+9\,2^p+6.
\]
Impose the single affine equation $Y_{11}+Y_{22}=1$.
Exactly six of the eight such $Y$ have rank one and two have rank two.
The slice therefore has size
\[
 6\,2^p+2,
\]
so rejection from the full fiber accepts with probability
\[
 \frac{6\,2^p+2}{2^{2p}+9\,2^p+6}\sim6\,2^{-p}.             \tag{14}
\]
Its one-dimensional reverse dual is spanned by the rank-two identity, so
the earlier rank-one-dual certificate does not apply. Formula (12) samples
this family with a constant two-character outer sum.

The audit instantiates $p=64$ and obtains direct exact samples. This is a
literal-coordinate control, not a claim that its raw source-free
recognition was run. Separate native examples below verify the full
recognition-to-sampling interface outside the old rank-one admission.
The two-condition example $Y_{11}=Y_{22}=1$ has size $2^p+3$ and is also
retained as a useful control.

## A. Positive sampling requires a proved conditional family

The acquired form is (h0+iota(v))(u)=y, with the complete original affine
bijection retained. X has p by d entries and Y has d by r entries over
F_(2^a); the right slice is binary affine of codimension c, not necessarily
linear over the extension field. The signed universal product fiber has an
explicit finite Gaussian double sum. The inherited independent derivation
instead applies row-space Mobius inversion; neither is an assumed oracle.
The reverse Hom pairing uses a nonzero functional annihilating commutators,
not the represented binary trace which may vanish at even multiplicity.

If t complete rows span A of rank alpha, quotient by A. The remaining
frequency rows must annihilate A. The free block and X-extension count is
q^[alpha(d-t)+p(t-alpha)]. Appending the next frequency row changes the two
relevant ranks in only three ways: (ell,rho), (ell+1,rho), (ell+1,rho+1).
Their domains are nested binary-linear preimages K contained in L contained
in E. The summand is (f0-f1)1_K+(f1-f2)1_L+f2 1_E. Each signed affine mass is
zero or a signed power of two, obtained by elimination. Consequently only
the original 2^c characters are summed, with no exponential prefix factor.

After the Fourier sum, integer nonnegative completion counts, not signed
terms, select the next bit. Branch ratios telescope to a uniform Y weighted
by its X fiber; an independent uniform affine solve for X gives the uniform
factor pair and then the original input. This proves acquired-row-prefix
sampling, not closure under arbitrary original-input pins. The native wrapper
checks 2^c against actual compact-description BYTES before preprocessing;
unrestricted c is still exponential. Exact unbiased integer draws have an
expected-time contract; optional seeded PRNG runs do not prove hardware or
information-theoretic randomness. The loose native expected O(L^29) bound is
not practical speed or bounded worst-case random-bit use.

statement: For binary X of shape p by2,Y of shape2 by2 and XY=0, full population is 2^(2p)+9*2^p+6. The rank-two character condition traceY=1 has population6*2^p+2, so full-fiber rejection succeeds asymptotically6*2^-p although c=1.
